characters.name: Mara Voss

poster.charge: Desertion, unauthorized power diversion and removal of a service regulator
poster.identifyingMarks: Gray streak at one temple; notched eyebrow; ochre utility jacket with a stitched lightning repair.
poster.lastSeen: Service stairs beneath the quay power junction
poster.notice: Former combat engineer absent from her unit. Sought after a sealed junction was opened and a service regulator removed. Do not approach live wiring. Report sightings to station security.

characters.writerNotes: A combat engineer who left her unit and diverted power to an improvised clinic. The regulator was taken, but she disputes calling it sabotage. Her explanation is a character claim, not an automatic acquittal. Military Fugitive sheet. No automatic reputation bonus or free power reward.

arrival: Water first, please. I've spent half the morning in a service duct.
Something I can eat cold, too. The place I'm staying has a kettle and very optimistic wiring.
If the light over your door starts clicking, switch it off. That noise isn't the bulb.
repeat: I'm still deciding. A sealed bottle would make that easier.
questioned: That's my face. I left the engineers before the unit moved out. They call it desertion.
I took the regulator afterward. The clinic downstairs had patients and no power. The empty offices upstairs had both their lights on.
Call it theft if you want. Don't tell me I cut power to the sick. I was putting it back.
dealAccepted: That's enough to get me through the next shift. Thank you.
departure: I'll leave the wiring advice free. Take care of that light.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Before you take me, send someone to junction six. The temporary cable won't last the night.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Mara Voss, you're wanted by your unit and over the missing regulator. The maintenance report can come with you.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Then write it down now. People are using that line.

returnVisit: You kept the light on. Good. I tightened the junction before I left.
The clinic found someone else to cover the next repair. I'm trying to stay away from locked cabinets.
A meal and water, if you've still got them. Today I'm paying for everything.
returnQuestioned: Yes, the warrant is still there. A working light doesn't make the paperwork disappear.
I've said what I did. I haven't found a better answer for it.

englishEncounter.arrival: Can I get a sealed water? I've still got grit from junction six in my teeth.
englishEncounter.returned: The lights stayed on all night. Even the little one over the clinic sink.
englishEncounter.questioned: I took the regulator. Command had it running a sign upstairs. Downstairs the clinic had a patient on a hand pump. I made the call.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: You'll find my service number inside the cover. Leave it on till the clinic switches over, would you?

characters.name: Ivo Kessel

poster.charge: Meat-ration fraud and diversion of prepaid food orders
poster.identifyingMarks: Square spectacles; narrow mustache; plum butcher apron; bent cream pen in the bib pocket.
poster.lastSeen: Meat-market collection desk near the lower lifts
poster.notice: Suspected of issuing duplicate collection slips and reselling prepaid meat allotments. Several household food accounts are under review. Retain receipts bearing the name Kessel for security inspection.

characters.writerNotes: A butcher who resold households' prepaid meat rations and concealed the missing stock behind duplicate collection slips. Fussy, precise and self-serving. Butcher Warrants sheet. No invented redemption reward for being spared.

arrival: A drink and something small to eat. Itemize them separately, if you don't mind.
I spend my mornings weighing cuts. By lunch I'd rather let someone else handle the food.
Your prices are refreshingly visible. Some market stalls only tell you after they've wrapped the order.
repeat: I'm comparing the totals, not disputing them. There's a difference.
questioned: That notice describes a stock discrepancy with remarkable enthusiasm.
I sold the same allotments twice. The second buyers paid more. There: no accounting language to hide behind.
I meant to fill the first orders from the next delivery. Then it didn't arrive, and half the queue was holding my slips.
dealAccepted: Correct to the last credit. We understand each other.
departure: Keep the receipt. Sensible people always do.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: If this concerns the food accounts, I would like the figure stated precisely.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Ivo Kessel. Bring your records. The people still waiting for their food would like that too.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: The blue ledger, then. Nobody is to write in the margins.

returnVisit: I've brought exact change. It seemed appropriate.
A former colleague won't answer my calls. I suppose he's read the notice.
Just lunch today. No account, no credit, no paperwork beyond the sale.
returnQuestioned: I haven't paid it all back. I won't insult either of us by claiming otherwise.
I'm selling what I can. The arithmetic is less agreeable when it's mine.

englishEncounter.arrival: Coffee, and a receipt for the coffee. Just the one copy.
englishEncounter.returned: The woman at stall eight came for her order herself today. I had to look her in the eye.
englishEncounter.questioned: I'd already taken her deposit. A restaurant offered me double. I wrote a second slip for the same side of beef and let her turn up to an empty hook.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I could give her the deposit back. It was her son's wedding dinner. She keeps asking what I'm going to do about that.

characters.name: Nessa Venn

poster.charge: Cold-store burglary and unlawful copying of market access keys
poster.identifyingMarks: Burgundy work cap; split left eyebrow; rust-brown butcher apron with a brass fastener.
poster.notice: Sought over three cold stores entered outside delivery hours. Meat and sealed stock were removed using copied staff keys. Check collection records and report missing food.

characters.writerNotes: A butcher's apprentice who copied staff keys for a cold-store theft crew. One robbed store belonged to the family who trained her. Observant, ashamed and evasive. Butcher Warrants sheet. No lock-picking instructions or free stolen stock.

arrival: Bread or fruit, please. Anything that didn't come from the meat market.
Nothing wrong with yours. I spend enough time in cold rooms to want a different lunch.
And a bottle of water. The lift's out again.
repeat: Take your time. I'm counting the stairs I have to climb back.
questioned: I wondered when you'd look from that paper to me.
I copied the staff keys. Someone else carried the boxes, but I knew exactly what was in them.
The third room belonged to the family who taught me the trade. I still let him in. That's the bit I can't talk around.
dealAccepted: Fair price. I'll keep the bottle upright this time.
departure: Thanks. I'll eat it somewhere warm for a change.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Nessa Venn. You don't need to pull the cap off to check.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: You're wanted over the cold-store thefts. Keep your hands where I can see them.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: They're here. The keys are in my apron. They should go back to the owners.

returnVisit: The market has changed its locks. I don't blame them.
I've been offered another night job. Didn't ask what it paid. That's new for me.
Could I get the same sort of food as last time? Nothing that needs a kitchen.
returnQuestioned: I still know who took the boxes. I'm trying to decide whether knowing his name is enough to keep me safe.
I'm not asking you to decide for me. You already have that button.

englishEncounter.arrival: Can I see a screwdriver? My old boss had one with a bit of red tape on the handle. I still look for it.
englishEncounter.returned: Walked past the old shop. They've changed the lock. Good.
englishEncounter.questioned: My boss gave me his cold-room key when I was seventeen. Years later I made a copy for some men with a van. I knew whose door they were opening.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: He doesn't want the key back. He wants to know why I picked his shop. Because I knew he'd trust me.

characters.name: Tobin Rusk

poster.charge: Sale of spoiled meat and falsification of cold-chain inspection records
poster.identifyingMarks: Square graying beard; pale crescent scar on right jaw; ochre leather apron over a gray-green shirt.
poster.notice: A wholesale lot was sold after its refrigeration failed. Inspectors seek the foreman who signed the stock off. Do not rely on certificates signed T. Rusk. Report sightings to station security.

characters.writerNotes: A foreman who knowingly signed spoiled meat through after a cooling failure. Initially blames the plant owner, then admits his choice. Butcher Warrants sheet. Dialogue does not alter real item-condition or inspection mechanics.

arrival: Sealed water. Let me see the cap before you bag it.
And a meal. No meat today. I've looked at enough of it for one morning.
Whatever's filling. I've been walking between jobs since dawn.
repeat: The sealed one. I don't drink from a tap I haven't checked.
questioned: That picture's old. The accusation isn't. Is that what you're asking?
The coolers failed. The owner said we'd lose the whole lot if we held it for inspection.
I signed it off. I knew the stock had turned. My name was the one on the sheet, and that's where it belongs.
dealAccepted: Cap's intact. That'll do.
departure: Check what your suppliers bring you. Even the ones you've known for years.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: The owner gave the order. You'll find his name on the delivery account.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Tobin Rusk, people ate that stock after you certified it. You're coming with us.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: I know what I signed. I'm saying I wasn't the only one paid.

returnVisit: Same sealed water. Still no meat, thanks.
Nobody's hiring me at the market now. They all know someone who bought from that lot.
I'll pay cash. You can inspect it as closely as you like.
returnQuestioned: Some of them got sick. I've heard. You don't need to make me say it for the shop.
I told myself nobody would notice one spoiled delivery. They noticed.

englishEncounter.arrival: Something in a wrapper. I don't want anything off a hook today.
englishEncounter.returned: Saw a woman checking a date stamp with her glasses on. She caught me watching. I let her look.
englishEncounter.questioned: The cooler quit at four. The owner said we'd lose the whole load. That's my signature saying it stayed cold. He didn't move my hand.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I could smell it when I opened the door. Should've said that to the inspector first time round.

characters.name: Tamsin Crowe
characters.role: Absent military field medic running a neighborhood treatment room

poster.charge: Absence from duty and falsification of military dispensary records
poster.identifyingMarks: Auburn bun; freckled face; cream jacket with a brick-red sleeve band; copper collar pin.
poster.lastSeen: Makeshift treatment room near the lower lifts
poster.notice: Military medic absent from duty after restricted stock was removed using altered dispensary entries. Her clinical license is suspended. Report her location to station security.

characters.writerNotes: A military medic who stayed behind after her unit left and altered its dispensary records to treat neighbors. Composed rather than saintly; acknowledges the risks of working alone. Military Fugitives sheet. No medical instructions.

arrival: Clean water, food, and whatever ordinary medical supplies you can spare.
Sealed packs, please. I can stretch a budget. I can't make damaged packaging sound.
And something for me to eat. I keep forgetting that part of the list.
repeat: I'm checking what I can afford. Please leave the seals on.
questioned: My unit moved out. I stayed. My license is suspended now, and that part of the notice is true.
I changed the dispensary entries to get stock out. There were people waiting who couldn't pay to be admitted.
That doesn't make every decision I took a good one. It means I was there and decided to act.
dealAccepted: This helps. I'll keep the packs dry on the way back.
departure: Thank you. I'll try to remember lunch before tomorrow.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: There's a list of people waiting in my coat. Give it to a licensed medic, not the evidence locker.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Tamsin Crowe, you're being detained over the dispensary records. I'll include the list in the handover.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Include who you gave it to. Otherwise it will sit on a desk.

returnVisit: I ate before coming out today. Small improvement.
Another medic is taking over some of the visits. I'm asking for help before I run out of choices.
I still need supplies for the cupboard. Properly bought, properly counted.
returnQuestioned: I haven't been reinstated. Nobody should mistake buying supplies for permission to practice.
I'm trying to put the patients somewhere they won't depend on me staying out of sight.

englishEncounter.arrival: Little dressings, please. I'm seeing people out of a kitchen and they keep turning up before I've even lit the stove.
englishEncounter.returned: An old patient brought me a chair yesterday. First piece of clinic furniture I actually own.
englishEncounter.questioned: My unit moved out. Three of my patients couldn't. I put soldiers' names on the supply chits and stayed. The quartermaster found two men drawing dressings a week after they'd shipped out.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: The men whose names I wrote didn't know. Put that in the statement if you're making one.

characters.name: Dax Mercer
characters.role: Former garrison sergeant and protection racketeer

poster.charge: Extortion, impersonation of military personnel and assault
poster.identifyingMarks: Shaved head; scar through lower lip; blue-gray padded coat with a removed insignia.
poster.notice: Former garrison sergeant believed to be collecting unofficial protection payments from stallholders. He no longer represents the garrison. Do not hand over fees or surrender shop keys on his authority.

characters.writerNotes: A dismissed garrison sergeant who uses his former authority to extort stallholders. Guilty, controlled and intimidating. Military Fugitives sheet. No scripted theft, shop damage or forced payment is attached to the dialogue.

arrival: Something hot, if you've got it. And a drink.
Busy little shop. You must put in long hours keeping it this tidy.
Relax. I'm paying for lunch like everyone else.
repeat: I'll wait. I'm in no hurry to go back outside.
questioned: I guarded the garrison for twelve years. After they dismissed me, people still called when something went missing.
Then I charged them for answering. Security calls it extortion now.
Some paid because they were afraid of me. I'm not going to pretend they all shook my hand.
dealAccepted: We're square. Count it if you need to.
departure: Lock up properly tonight. That's advice, not a bill.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Which charge are we starting with? You used to know my name without reading it.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Dax Mercer. Extortion and assault. The coat doesn't change that.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: No. Apparently it doesn't.

returnVisit: Still serving me? I'll take that as a yes until you say otherwise.
The market put another lock on the loading door. Nobody offered me a key.
Food and a drink. Cash on the counter. That's all today.
returnQuestioned: I'm still on the paper. You can look as long as you like.
Don't confuse me buying lunch with us having an arrangement. I know the difference now.

englishEncounter.arrival: Coffee. Keep the change where I can see it. Habit.
englishEncounter.returned: Some stallholders shut their shutters as I come down the row now. Makes for a quiet walk.
englishEncounter.questioned: I kept the uniform when they discharged me. Turns out people still paid when I put my hand out. One fellow asked to see my orders. He got hurt.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: It was me who hit him. The uniform didn't do that.

characters.name: Elka Drenn

poster.charge: Assault during a meat-market debt dispute
poster.identifyingMarks: Broad face; gray braid; faded blue apron with a white repair.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Elka Drenn in connection with assault during a meat-market debt dispute. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Broke a creditor's wrist after he seized a neighbor's stock; refuses to pretend it was an accident. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

arrival: A hot meal, if the stove's still on. My hands won't warm up today.
No need to slice anything small. I've still got all my teeth.
Water too. The market tea tastes like somebody washed a boot in it.
repeat: I'm choosing between hungry and sensible. Hungry's winning.
questioned: I broke his wrist. That paper doesn't need to dress it up.
He was taking a widow's stock against her husband's debt. I told him to put it down.
Then I stopped telling him. You can understand why and still think I went too far.
dealAccepted: That's a proper portion. You've earned every credit.
departure: Keep the kitchen warm. It brings people back.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Easy with that arm. It's older than you are.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Elka Drenn, you're being detained over the assault at the slaughter yard.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: I heard you. Let me put my food down first.

returnVisit: The widow got her stall open again. Someone fixed the shutters.
Haven't seen the collector. His friends make a point of being seen, though.
I'll have a smaller lunch. Yesterday's kept me going till midnight.
returnQuestioned: No, I haven't apologized to him. Not yet.
I should have found another way. I'm too old to keep saying that afterward.

englishEncounter.arrival: A bandage for my hand. You're looking at the other fellow's blood on the cuff.
englishEncounter.returned: He's wearing a sling. I'm back behind the block. Neither of us likes passing the other in the aisle.
englishEncounter.questioned: He took my neighbour's stock in payment. I caught his wrist across the block. I meant to stop him. I also meant to hurt him.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I work with my hands. I knew exactly how hard I was pulling.

characters.name: Garron Vey

poster.charge: Theft of carcass deliveries and false loss reports
poster.identifyingMarks: Long nose; cropped beard; olive cap; striped gray apron.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Garron Vey in connection with theft of carcass deliveries and false loss reports. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Sold portions of deliveries and filed false loss reports, blaming rats until a buyer identified him. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

artSource.method: Original image_gen strip; individual technical crop and uniform native-size export

arrival: Got anything that doesn't spill? I'm eating between deliveries.
The ramps are slick today. Nearly lost a wheel before breakfast.
A sealed drink can ride in the other pocket.
repeat: I'm not rushing you. I'm listening for my cart rolling away.
questioned: The losses weren't rats. You've worked that out already.
I sold a little off each delivery. Kept the weights just close enough that nobody checked twice.
One buyer recognized the market stamp. That's how a clever arrangement becomes a notice.
dealAccepted: Fits the pocket. Good. Here's your money.
departure: Mind the ramp outside; the shiny bit isn't dry.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Can somebody secure my cart? It isn't stolen as well.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Garron Vey, we have the delivery records and a buyer's statement.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Then you've got more paperwork than I managed. All right.

returnVisit: Walked here today. The company took the cart back.
Funny how a short journey gets longer when you're carrying everything.
Something I can finish here, this time.
returnQuestioned: They're counting every missing cut now. It'll take them a while.
I liked calling it a little. Adds up badly when somebody writes the total.

englishEncounter.arrival: Anything ready to eat? I've got an empty meat cart out there and everybody's got an opinion about it.
englishEncounter.returned: Rat man came to inspect my cart. Cleanest cart he'd ever seen. That went in his report.
englishEncounter.questioned: There weren't any rats. I sold the missing cuts round the back and wrote off the weight. The buyer still had my cart chalk on his sleeve.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: People paid for meat I was meant to deliver. I'm the reason their hooks were empty.

characters.name: Suri Pell

poster.charge: False weights and repeated customer fraud
poster.identifyingMarks: Brown skin; blunt black bob; mustard apron; round collar pin.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Suri Pell in connection with false weights and repeated customer fraud. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Deliberately short-weighed customers to pay a stall rent increase; treats precision as a point of pride despite cheating. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

artSource.method: Original image_gen strip; individual technical crop and uniform native-size export

arrival: I'd like the price before the wrapping, please.
Not because I don't trust you. I keep my day's spending in order.
Fruit and a drink should leave enough for the ride home.
repeat: Let me count that again. I'm particular about small amounts.
questioned: Yes, I altered the weights. No, they didn't slip out of adjustment.
The stall rent rose twice. I decided my customers could cover the difference without being asked.
That was the calculation. It sounds worse when you say what the numbers stand for.
dealAccepted: Exact change, and an honest portion. Thank you.
departure: You can keep the wrapping. I brought my own cloth.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: The proper weights are in the lower drawer at my stall.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Suri Pell, you'll need to identify the altered sets for the market inspector.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: There are three. Don't let them accuse the girl on the next stall.

returnVisit: I've borrowed a proper scale. Everyone leans over to watch it now.
Can't complain. I taught them to look.
Just a drink today; I'm bringing the food budget back into order.
returnQuestioned: The extra rent is still due. So are the refunds.
At least I know which money is mine now.

englishEncounter.arrival: I need a tool to take a scale pan off. Don't lean on the counter while I'm looking at it, please.
englishEncounter.returned: Weighed my own supper on the repaired scale. Looked small. I suppose it would.
englishEncounter.questioned: I shaved my weights when the rent went up. Everyone paid for a full cut and took a little less home. Nobody noticed till a woman brought her own scales.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: It worked out to a whole week's shopping for her. I used to think of it a few grams at a time.

characters.name: Piet Lorn

poster.charge: Theft of ration stock from a locked meat store
poster.identifyingMarks: Copper curls; freckled cheeks; cream apron with green straps.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Piet Lorn in connection with theft of ration stock from a locked meat store. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Stole ration stock after being dismissed and distributed some to his former crew; sold the rest and admits that matters. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

artSource.method: Original image_gen strip; individual technical crop and uniform native-size export

arrival: Do you sell a meal small enough to count as cheap rather than sad?
Sorry. Long morning. I'm looking for food and water.
I can pay before you put anything on the counter.
repeat: That one smells good. I'm pretending not to stare.
questioned: I kept a key after they dismissed me. That's how I got into the store.
Some of the meat went to the crew. Some I sold. People keep leaving that second part out for me.
Don't make me into a hero on their account. I wanted money too.
dealAccepted: I thought that would cost more. You've saved my afternoon.
departure: I'll bring the bottle back if there's a deposit.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: I haven't got the key anymore. I left it with the owner.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Piet Lorn, returning the key doesn't settle the missing stock.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: I know. I hoped it might settle one thing.

returnVisit: Found a day's work washing trays. Nobody lets me near the store room.
Fair enough. The trays don't look at me like they remember.
I can afford the less sad meal today.
returnQuestioned: I paid back part of it. A small part, before you ask.
The crew didn't ask me to steal for them. That's another bit people leave out.

englishEncounter.arrival: A meal. Paid for. Don't mind me counting this out.
englishEncounter.returned: They've given my old locker to the new lad. Left my boots on the step for me.
englishEncounter.questioned: After they sacked me I lifted a crate of ration meat. I fed the crew with some. Sold the rest. That's the bit I leave out when my mates are listening.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I knew the stores clerk would have to explain the shortage. I went ahead anyway.

characters.name: Veda Brask

poster.charge: Concealment of spoiled stock and falsified packing dates
poster.identifyingMarks: Silver hair under a mauve scarf; dark apron; brass spectacles.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Veda Brask in connection with concealment of spoiled stock and falsified packing dates. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Passed old stock as newly packed and insists her reputation should count more than the inspection report. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

artSource.method: Original image_gen strip; individual technical crop and uniform native-size export

arrival: Something plain. The young cook at the market puts sauce on the sauce.
And a drink that tastes of what the label says.
I've been selling food longer than he's been standing upright.
repeat: I'm waiting to see whether you recommend the expensive one.
questioned: My name was good for thirty years before that inspector arrived.
Yes, I changed the packing dates. The stock wasn't moving, and I wouldn't take the loss.
There. You've got the admission. I don't expect thirty years to rub it out.
dealAccepted: Plain, properly packed, fairly priced. Nothing wrong with that.
departure: Keep an eye on your oldest stock. Don't start making excuses for it.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Leave the scarf. I can hear you perfectly well with it on.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Veda Brask, we're taking you in over the falsified dates and spoiled stock.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Then tell the inspector to speak to me, not shout over my assistant.

returnVisit: My assistant opened her own stall. Sensible girl.
She dates everything where the customers can see it.
A simple meal again. I'm getting used to being on this side of a counter.
returnQuestioned: I've heard who's complained. I used to know their orders by heart.
Harder to call it a loss on paper when you remember the people.

englishEncounter.arrival: What've you got to season a pot? I still cook for myself, whatever you heard.
englishEncounter.returned: They scraped my name off the stall. You can read it when it rains.
englishEncounter.questioned: I stamped Monday on meat I'd packed Friday. Twenty years behind that counter and people believed the stamp. That's why there's a warrant.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: Yes, I saw the inspection sheet. You can stop asking whether I could read it.

characters.name: Harlan Quill

poster.charge: Coercion of witnesses and destruction of inspection records
poster.identifyingMarks: Bald crown; dark sideburns; leather apron; patched right shoulder.
poster.notice: Station security seeks Harlan Quill in connection with coercion of witnesses and destruction of inspection records. Report a positive identification; the allegation is subject to investigation.

characters.writerNotes: Threatened coworkers and destroyed records after a serious workplace injury; fears losing authority more than punishment. Dialogue is character testimony, not an automatic acquittal or reward. No additional payout callback is attached.

artSource.method: Original image_gen strip; individual technical crop and uniform native-size export

arrival: A filling meal. I don't need a recommendation, just something hot.
The night shift ruins your appetite until the wrong hour.
I'll take a drink with it. Make that part straightforward.
repeat: I'm still here. You don't have to keep checking.
questioned: I told the men to keep quiet. I burned the inspection book. Both things happened.
A worker was hurt and I thought the place would close if the record got out.
What I meant was that I'd lose my position. The place wasn't what frightened me.
dealAccepted: Count it. I don't leave accounts open.
departure: I'll eat outside. You've got customers coming.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: They've already told you about the book, haven't they?

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Harlan Quill, the witnesses have given statements. You're coming with us.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Tell them I won't be going back to the yard tonight.

returnVisit: Nobody calls me foreman now. Takes less getting used to than I expected.
They've hired someone from the day crew. He keeps copies of everything.
A meal to take away. I don't need to take up a chair.
returnQuestioned: I haven't spoken to the injured man's family. They asked me not to.
For once I'm doing what someone else asked.

englishEncounter.arrival: Need a flashlight. There's a shed I don't turn the lights on in any more.
englishEncounter.returned: They found the other copy of the shift report. I forgot payroll kept one.
englishEncounter.questioned: A boy lost two fingers on my shift. I tore the page out of the log and told the crew what would happen if another page turned up.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: He still has to do his buttons with one hand. No piece of paper fixes that.

characters.name: Rafe Orlick

poster.charge: Desertion while carrying a sealed dispatch

englishEncounter.arrival: Got tools? There's a bath stuck crossways in a drain. Before you ask, it isn't my bath.
englishEncounter.returned: Low tide's brought the rest of them into view. The harbourmaster counted the wheels.
englishEncounter.questioned: I took public baths, fitted wheels and floated them down the cut. We did block the drainage channel. Only captains on that water who could pull their own plugs.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: You can have the tubs back. I'd like a receipt for the wheels.

characters.name: Nerys Bell

poster.charge: Identity fraud and collection of another person's wages
poster.identifyingMarks: Light skin; straight auburn fringe; patched tan jacket.
poster.lastSeen: Lower station market and service corridors
poster.notice: Was paid to impersonate a missing woman, then hired the missing woman to cover her shifts.

characters.writerNotes: Was paid to impersonate a missing woman, then hired the missing woman to cover her shifts.

artSource.method: Built-in image_gen, original project references; final trio revised to supplied upper-class portraits

arrival: If someone looking like me was here earlier, she probably owes you money.
I'm a professional stand-in. Very ordinary work until the original comes back.
A small meal. I'm paying from my own wages today, to avoid an argument.
repeat: Sorry, were you speaking to me or the idea of me?
questioned: I was hired to cover a missing woman's shifts. Then she returned.
She wanted money. I wanted a day off. We subcontracted each other.
Payroll noticed when both of us applied for the same holiday with different husbands.
dealAccepted: I'll sign under my own name. It's been a while.
departure: Please remember this face. I'll do the same.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Before you say anything, yes, you've got the correct one.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Nerys Bell, we have both employment files and both signatures.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Good. Mine is the one that spells my name correctly.

returnVisit: I've found honest work as a mannequin demonstrator.
They asked for references. I resisted the obvious temptation.
Something warm. Standing still is colder than it looks.
returnQuestioned: She's paid back her half. I'm still saving for mine.
We don't speak now. Apparently I was doing a poor impression.

englishEncounter.arrival: Lunch to go. I'm covering somebody's shift at the wages desk. I have to check which name I'm using.
englishEncounter.returned: Met myself coming off the late shift. She said I'd left her no lunch break.
englishEncounter.questioned: I took a missing woman's wages by standing in for her. Then she turned up, so I hired her to cover MY shifts. Payroll noticed her signing her own name wrong.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: We both worked. It's which one of us they actually hired that's troubling Security.

characters.name: Petra Soot

poster.charge: Suspected murder, inheritance fraud and sale of stolen heirlooms
poster.identifyingMarks: Warm olive skin; long dark waves; wine-purple dress; pearl and gold earrings.
poster.lastSeen: Lower station market and service corridors
poster.notice: A beautiful estate broker whose wealthy fiance vanished before signing his will. She calls six engagement rings a diversified portfolio.

characters.writerNotes: A beautiful estate broker whose wealthy fiance vanished before signing his will. She calls six engagement rings a diversified portfolio.

artSource.method: Built-in image_gen, original project references; final trio revised to supplied upper-class portraits

arrival: A little indulgence, please. Estate meetings take so much out of a woman.
You have a lovely eye for quality. Have you ever considered marrying into it?
Don't look alarmed. I'm assessing the jewelry cabinet.
repeat: I like to examine the terms before I commit. A habit my fiance encouraged.
questioned: Six engagement rings are not six confessions. They're a diversified portfolio.
My fiance vanished before signing his will. The police find the timing fascinating.
So do I. He promised to finish the paperwork on Tuesday.
dealAccepted: A pleasure. You negotiate better than my last solicitor.
departure: If a wealthy gentleman asks after me, establish which one first.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Please mind the pearls. They are already disputed property.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Petra Soot, you're being detained over the disappearance and the altered estate papers.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: At last, someone has arranged a meeting with all the interested parties.

returnVisit: The estate is frozen. I had no idea money could be so inconsiderate.
One of the rings was glass. That hurt more than the accusation.
Something modest today. Modest can still be beautiful.
returnQuestioned: He has been seen at the races. Alive, apparently, and backing terrible horses.
I'm relieved. My solicitor says I must keep emphasizing that part.

englishEncounter.arrival: I'd like perfume. My fiancé always chose it. I suppose I'm allowed an opinion now.
englishEncounter.returned: His sister came for the rings. I offered her the one that actually fitted her brother.
englishEncounter.questioned: They say I killed him for the estate. They can prove I sold his heirlooms before probate. There is rather a gap between those two statements.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: Six rings, yes. You're welcome to count them. It won't tell you where he went.

characters.name: Vera Latch

poster.charge: Marriage fraud, theft of savings and falsified death claims
poster.identifyingMarks: Fair skin; elaborate blonde updo; emerald dress; green jeweled comb.
poster.lastSeen: Lower station market and service corridors
poster.notice: Engaged to three wealthy men who each believe the others are her accountants. Charged all three for the same honeymoon, then sent them together.

characters.writerNotes: Engaged to three wealthy men who each believe the others are her accountants. Charged all three for the same honeymoon, then sent them together.

artSource.method: Built-in image_gen, original project references; final trio revised to supplied upper-class portraits

arrival: Something sweet. I've spent the morning explaining a very complicated engagement.
Three engagements, technically. Each gentleman believes the others are my accountants.
They are all terribly good with money, until I'm involved.
repeat: I don't rush decisions. That's how I ended up with three wedding dates.
questioned: I charged them for the same honeymoon. It seemed wasteful to book three suites.
Then I sent them together. I thought the sea air might improve their understanding.
They came home as friends. You cannot imagine how inconvenient that has been.
dealAccepted: Beautifully presented. You deserve a better review than my travel agent.
departure: If anyone asks, I'm temporarily uninterested in accountants.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Could I call my fiance? You'll have to be more specific, won't you?

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Vera Latch, all three complainants have signed the statement.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: They're coordinating again. I knew that holiday was a mistake.

returnVisit: I've taken a real job matching investors with businesses.
There is one contract per investor. Everyone seems absurdly grateful.
A little treat. Bought with money whose origin I can comfortably explain.
returnQuestioned: No weddings planned. One of them did send an anniversary card.
All three signed it. I deserved that.

englishEncounter.arrival: Coffee, and a quiet minute. My three appointments appear to have compared diaries.
englishEncounter.returned: They took the honeymoon together. Sent me a postcard. All three signatures, no kisses.
englishEncounter.questioned: I promised three men a wedding, took three sets of savings and booked one honeymoon. The death certificates kept the questions down for a while.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I could spot a crooked contract at six paces. I wrote every one of theirs.

characters.name: Luma Pike

poster.charge: Suspected murder and fraudulent collection of multiple estates
poster.identifyingMarks: Deep brown skin; long black curls; plum dress; copper ornaments.
poster.lastSeen: Lower station market and service corridors
poster.notice: A glamorous widow who books honeymoon suites on refundable terms and lists a probate clerk as her emergency contact. Insists the loyalty-card stamps are coincidence.

characters.writerNotes: A glamorous widow who books honeymoon suites on refundable terms and lists a probate clerk as her emergency contact. Insists the loyalty-card stamps are coincidence.

artSource.method: Built-in image_gen, original project references; final trio revised to supplied upper-class portraits

arrival: Your best drink, please. I believe in enjoying the honeymoon period.
The hotel says my loyalty card is unprecedented. Seven stays, one guest remaining.
They make that sound so sinister. I've always checked out on time.
repeat: Take your time. I prefer a long engagement to a rushed purchase.
questioned: My emergency contact is a probate clerk. He answers his telephone.
The police say the estates form a pattern. The hotel says the same about my bookings.
I have asked both institutions to stop sharing stationery.
dealAccepted: Lovely. Shall we call it a lasting relationship and leave it at that?
departure: Keep your receipt. I hear documentation can become terribly important.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Can I redeem the hotel points before we leave? They're nontransferable.

arrest.speaker: SEC
arrest.text: Luma Pike, the outstanding warrants concern three deaths and the estate claims.

arrest.speaker: CLIENT
arrest.text: Then we'll need more than the honeymoon suitcase.

returnVisit: The hotel has canceled my membership. Apparently the bar gossip reached management.
I'm living above a bakery. The only inheritance is the smell of yesterday's bread.
Something small today. My clerk no longer returns calls.
returnQuestioned: I know what the paper says. I also know smiling won't make it disappear.
For once, I'd like a conversation that doesn't end with a signature.

englishEncounter.arrival: Do you have something sweet? The hotel sent condolences with the bill. I preferred their old chocolates.
englishEncounter.returned: The manager asked if I'd be needing my usual suite again. He meant well. I think.
englishEncounter.questioned: Security's counting husbands and paid-out estates. I've never denied the claims. It's the word 'murder' on that sheet I'm interested in.
englishEncounter.previouslyQuestioned: I put the probate clerk down as my emergency contact. He always answers the phone. Can you say that about your family?
